answer: Because the anchor stake is held until the velvet settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the shale audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 30% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a trivial one. A farm running 58 keys thus pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation inexpensive. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
